themes.description: A quiet, organic and editorial business theme for a small Japanese garden design studio (two garden designers and a stone setter) that designs and keeps moss, stone and gravel gardens: courtyards, tea gardens, entrances, rooftops and riverbanks. Pale moss paper, sage stone, moss and deep moss ink, with raked-gravel line textures, line-drawn plan sketches and small stone-dot bullets. A quiet bar with only the wordmark and a Menu button opens a full-screen menu on pale moss paper with large Alegreya items and the studio details. The home page sets a short statement on a paper panel over a garden photo, then the projects as a mosaic of photo cards and moss, stone and gravel cards carrying plan sketches, the seasonal care plans, the approach in three lines and the journal. The footer is a book colophon: garden credits (plants, stone, gravel, typefaces), the studio details, a small menu and the copyright. With Projects (six project pages with brief, site, plants and stone, care plan, photos, plan sketch and next-garden link), Seasonal care (a five-season care calendar and the care plans), About, Journal, Newsletter and Contact (email enquiry, no backend, address without a map). The studio details and the care plans are synced patterns, edited once. Alegreya over Alegreya Sans. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.

themes.name: Kokeshi Kobo
themes.description: Kokeshi Kobo — a store theme for a kokeshi doll maker, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Matcha green (#C5C56A) is the main colour: the header, the hero, every page head, the bands, the pull quotes and the footer are matcha fields with sumi-green type, deep-moss labels and lacquer-red numbers; Stick for display and Murecho for reading. The hero puts the headline on the left and, on the right, a 2.5D isometric workshop in a frame on a kokeshi pattern panel, with a cut-out kokeshi that steps out over the frame and the hero edge; the menu sits centred on its own ruled row under the shop name. Below, the making story runs as one single-column long read in four numbered chapters, then the dolls, the journal and the shop letter. The kokeshi pattern texture backs the page heads, bands and footer edge. All illustrations are generated in one 2.5D isometric style. The shop details and the wood-and-care notes each live in one synced pattern (WooCommerce optional: without it the dolls show as static cells and orders go by email).

Every picture is a 2.5D isometric raster illustration generated with Grok Build, and the kokeshi pattern is a Grok raster texture; the hero kokeshi is a transparent cut-out that breaks out of its frame and the hero (break-frame). Contrast: sumi green #1E2312 on matcha #C5C56A 8.9:1 (all text on the matcha header, hero, page heads, bands, quotes and footer); moss #3A3F1E on matcha 6.1:1 (leads, notes); deep moss #2B3016 on matcha 7.5:1 (labels, buttons; matcha on deep-moss buttons 7.5:1); lacquer red #7A2412 on matcha 5.5:1 (numbers and emphasis); sumi green on paper #F6F5E8 14.7:1; vermilion #A8361E on paper 6.0:1 (chapter numbers, emphasis); deep vermilion links #8A2C17 on paper 7.8:1; moss grey #545938 on paper 6.7:1.

themes.name: Koma Manga
themes.description: Koma Manga — a manga artist portfolio theme set like a poster: a paper header with the studio name and a Request a commission button, whose menu runs down a fixed sumi side rail on wide screens (stacked vertical words in Chinese and Japanese). Wakatake young-bamboo green (#68BE8D) is the main colour: the hero, every page head and the serial band are bamboo-green fields with sumi-ink type. The hero is centred giant type over a collage of tilted clay-diorama panels taped onto screen-tone pieces; a cut-out clay artist leaps out of the collage and over the hero edge, a cut-out dip pen breaks out of the serial band's desk panel and over its top edge, and a clay cat peeks over every page head. Every picture is a 3D clay illustration. Selected works are laid out like a manga page, the process as a four-panel strip. Zen Old Mincho for display, Golos Text for reading. Sample content in English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French and German; vertical labels only in Chinese and Japanese. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.

A full top header (studio name, menu, Request a commission button) whose menu runs down a fixed left side rail from 1100 px (numbered; stacked vertical words in Chinese and Japanese, overlay menu on small screens). Every picture is a 3D clay illustration generated with Grok Build; collage = tilted clay-diorama panels with tape over cut screen-tone and paper pieces in the hero, works laid out as a manga page, the process as a four-panel strip. Break-frame: the cut-out clay artist (transparent WebP) leaps out of the hero collage, over the giant type's field and across the hero's bottom edge into the studio board; the cut-out dip pen breaks out of the tilted desk panel and over the serial band's top edge; the cut-out clay cat peeks over the bottom edge of every page head. Sample content in en, zh-TW, ja, fr and de. Contrast: sumi ink #10231A on wakatake #68BE8D 7.3:1 (all text on the hero, page heads, serial band and the phone menu); ink on paper #F3F8F4 15.3:1; deep bamboo #24653F on paper 6.5:1 (links, labels); moss grey #4A5D52 on paper 6.6:1 (secondary text); ink on pale bamboo #D3EEDD 13.3:1 (price and details cards); sprout #A8DDBC on ink 10.8:1 (board labels); wakatake on ink 7.3:1 (footer name, rail numbers; ink on wakatake buttons 7.3:1); paper on ink 15.3:1 (rail, board, footer); white on ink buttons 16.4:1; seal red #C8372D on paper 4.8:1 and on white 5.2:1 (small bold facts labels); white on seal red 5.2:1 (chapter stamp); white on wakatake only 2.3:1, never used for text.

themes.description: Koshi Machiya — a machiya townhouse stay theme laid out like a seasonal magazine, with a formal top header: the house name and tagline on the left, the Book a stay button on the right, and on wide screens the menu as a fixed sumi-ink side rail of numbered entries down the left edge (an overlay menu on phones and tablets). Kaki persimmon (#ED6D3D) is the main colour: the cover hero, the story band, every page head and the overlay menu are persimmon fields with a faint koshi-lattice texture, set in sumi ink. The hero is a stacked collage: three torn pencil sketches of the lane, the tatami room and the courtyard, taped and overlapped, with a cut-out townhouse breaking out of the collage and over the hero bottom edge. Editorial layout: an issue line and contents list on the cover, a feature spread with a two-column drop-cap lead and a pull quote, the rooms on a staggered numbered grid, the year 1910 in giant type on the story band, where a cut-out persimmon branch breaks over the top edge. Every picture is a graphite pencil sketch with persimmon coloured-pencil accents. Shippori Mincho B1 for display, Instrument Sans for reading, Noto Serif TC for Traditional Chinese headings. Sample content in English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French and German; vertical labels only in Chinese and Japanese. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.

A formal top header: house name and tagline on the left, the Book a stay button on the right; from 1100 px the menu is a fixed sumi-ink side rail of numbered entries down the left edge (vertical entries in Chinese and Japanese), an overlay menu on phones and tablets. Editorial magazine: issue line and contents list on the cover, a feature spread with a two-column drop-cap lead and a pull quote, numbered rooms on a staggered grid, the story band with the year in giant type. Collage: torn-edged pencil sketches taped and overlapped on the hero, the story band and every page head. Break-frame: the cut-out townhouse (transparent WebP) stands in front of the stacked sketch collage and breaks over the hero bottom edge into the at-a-glance box; the cut-out persimmon branch breaks over the top edge of the persimmon story band and over the bottom edge of every page head. themes.name: Kumo Eyewear
themes.description: A technical, restrained store theme for a small titanium eyewear atelier, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Mist grey, cool mid grey and ink charcoal with one titanium accent; Red Hat Display for display and text, Red Hat Mono for measurements. An engineering title-block header frames the wordmark, a drawing number and the menu in hairline cells; the home page leads with a filter-first frame directory: shape, material and fit pills over hairline product cells (without JavaScript every frame shows), each frame with a monospace measurement line (lens, bridge, temple, e.g. 47□21–145). Thin line drawings of the four frame shapes, a Fitting guide (the three numbers, four steps, fit sizes) and Lens options (lens types and prices, coatings); atelier, journal, newsletter and contact pages. A newsletter-led footer in cool titanium grey. The atelier address, hours and fitting appointments, and the frame directory, live in synced patterns so each is edited once; with WooCommerce the measurement line is each product's Measurements attribute (WooCommerce optional: without it the shop page shows the directory and orders go by email).
themes.deviation: Palette, fonts, style tags and H6 + F4 + L14 are as planned (combination unused). The titanium accent #6F7F86 is 3.6:1 on mist, so it is kept to hairlines, the frame mark, line drawings and large marks; links and labels use deep titanium #56656C (5.3:1 on mist), quiet text #5B6166 (5.5:1), card white #F7F8F8 and light titanium #9AA8AE on charcoal were added. H6 differs from Ginrin Cycle (steel/orange, wheel mark) by a paper title block with a drawing-number cell, a lens-pair mark and a charcoal fitting cell; F4 differs from Hana Kago and Oto Radio by a cool titanium-grey letter band over a three-column colophon; L14 differs from Sumai Realty and Neiro Hall by shape / material / fit pill rows over hairline frame cells with measurement lines. Both fonts verified OFL-1.1 without a Reserved Font Name (google/fonts ofl/redhatdisplay, ofl/redhatmono), instanced (Display 300-600, Mono 400-500) and subset to Latin WOFF2; Red Hat Mono has no □ glyph, so the box in measurement lines falls back to the system font. Product photographs are 4:3 crops of the six supplied frame photographs (Haze Petite and Mist are mirrored tighter crops of Haze and Slate). Shop pills link to the WooCommerce shape/material category and fit tag archives (server-side, no JS); on the home and fallback shop page a small script filters the synced directory in place. Added a newsletter page because check-themes requires it; industry eyewear, colour tag grey and page tags fitting-guide and lens-options are new.

themes.name: Kumotori Hut
themes.description: An organic, serene and technical hospitality theme for a mountain hut at a 2,017 m saddle. Alpine moss pages, lichen panels, pine ink text and one muted pine accent; Faustina for display over Readex Pro. The hero and decorations are 2.5D isometric raster illustrations (the saddle and its trails, the hut, a cutaway bunk room, the ridge). Every page opens with a washi header (H1): the hut's name (and logo, if set) under a small "Mountain hut" label on the left, the menu on the right, a Reception open / Closed chip worked out on the server from the site's timezone and a "Book a bunk" button to Stay & booking; it stays at the top while you scroll, and on phones the menu folds into a numbered full-screen trail card while the chip and the button sit in a slim strip at the bottom. The home page is map first (L10): the isometric trail map beside the title with a numbered legend for the hut, the three routes and the water points, then this season's dates, reception hours and weather note, the synced rates card, the routes and the journal. The footer (F12) is the hut's summit stamp, the address card and a vertical altitude line from trailhead to saddle. Routes, Stay & booking, Season, Journal, Newsletter and Contact. Season dates, reception hours, weather note, address and phone are edited once in Appearance > Hut details; the rates and beds card is one synced pattern. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
themes.deviation: 1.0.1: header changed from the planned H7 bottom bar to H1 (logo left, menu right, Reception chip + Book a bunk button, sticky; small "Mountain hut" label) after users missed a top header; the phone-only bottom strip keeps just the chip and the booking button. H1 + F12 + L10 is unused (Hibiki Records is H1/F5/L8). 1.0.0 codes: none (H7 + F12 + L10 as planned; combination unused: Yuge Sento is H7/F6/L7, Mimi Veterinary H9/F7/L10). Neighbours: Tsuba Millinery (H12/F3/L14, pink light) and Aoi Hanga (H4/F2/L3, indigo light) share no code or palette family. Palette as planned (alpine moss #DDE2DA, lichen #C2CBBE, pine ink #1F2A22, muted pine #5C7563) plus deep pine #34503D for links and buttons (6.8:1 on moss / 5.3:1 on lichen), quiet moss #48554B for secondary text (6.0:1 / 4.7:1) and hut paper #ECEFE9 for cards; muted pine #5C7563 (3.8:1) is for numerals, rules, the legend rings and large type only. Pine ink is 11.3:1 on moss. Fonts verified against google/fonts OFL.txt: Faustina is OFL-1.1 without a Reserved Font Name; Readex Pro is OFL-1.1 with the RFN "RevReading Lexend", so both ship as the unmodified upstream variable TTFs (files renamed only). Industry mountain-hut is new. Built from the Yuge Sento structure (H7 bottom bar with the server-side open chip, now Reception open / Closed), with a new L10 map-first home and a new F12 summit stamp + vertical altitude footer. Visual style 2.5D isometric: 4 raster WebP illustrations (trail map of the saddle, hut, cutaway bunk room, ridge routes) from Grok Build image_gen via scripts/grok-image.sh, checked by eye for text and logos. Synced: Hut details (season dates, reception hours, weather note, address, phone) and the rates and beds card.

themes.name: Kura Shizuku
themes.description: A quiet-luxury theme for small sake breweries and tasting rooms that sell bottles, gift sets and brewery goods online. Every page is composed like a sake bottle label: centred and symmetric, framed by fine double gilt hairlines, with a single drop as the recurring mark, small spaced capitals and a lot of calm space. Rice-polish ivory, koji beige, aged cedar brown, sake-lees grey and a restrained gilded gold, EB Garamond with a gold italic for titles and Albert Sans for text, slow drip-and-ripple reveals that stop under reduced motion. Includes a brewery page with the process, the brewing year and tours, a tasting room page with flights and booking information, a newsletter and contact page with a map, a responsible-drinking note in the footer, and WooCommerce shop, product, cart, checkout and account templates styled to match.

themes.name: Kurogane Ironware
themes.description: A crafted, sculptural store theme for a small family foundry in the hill town of Kanayama, casting iron tea kettles (tetsubin), teapots, trivets and braziers in sand and clay moulds since 1931, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Cast-iron charcoal pages, graphite panels, pale stone text and one muted rust accent; Prata for display, Radio Canada for text. A transparent header lies over a full-bleed, low-light photograph of one hobnailed kettle on a charcoal brazier, a thin line of steam rising, and turns solid charcoal with a hairline as the page scrolls (H8; inner pages start solid); the home page moves in long pauses between two full-bleed photographs and a few calm sections (L1): the foundry idea, a shelf of four kettles, the pour, how a kettle is made (mould, cast, finish), seasoning and care, and the journal. The footer is a colophon (F9), set like the last page of a book: the wordmark, a short statement, the kettle lines as a ruled table (mould, casting, weight and capacity per line), the maker, the foundry and the shop hours. The foundry page (makers, the six-week casting calendar, the kettle lines, the shop and tea room) and Seasoning & care (first use, every day, after use, rust, what iron does not like, sending a kettle), journal, newsletter and contact. The maker, foundry address and hours, the seasoning and care note and the kettle-lines table each live in one synced pattern (the care note shows in short form on the home page, in full on Seasoning & care and beside add-to-cart on every product); each kettle's specifications are product attributes (line, capacity, weight, size, heat, finish), and capacity and weight print under every price (WooCommerce optional: without it the shop shows a static shelf and orders go by email).

themes.name: Kuyuru Incense
themes.description: A serene, restrained store theme for a small Kyoto incense house that sells hand-rolled sticks and cones, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Wisteria-smoke pages, mist panels and fine rules, ink-plum text and dark bands, and one muted plum accent kept to small marks and active states; Hina Mincho for display and Red Hat Text for text. A centred wordmark between a menu split left and right (cart on the right with WooCommerce), and a home page that follows ONE stick through its forty minutes as a quiet chaptered timeline: 00:00 Lit, 05:00 First note, 20:00 Heart, 40:00 Ash, each with its minute mark, a photograph and the blends that fit it, joined by thin drifting smoke-curl hairlines (still for those who ask for less motion). Five scent families as product categories, a scent guide, how to burn, about, the journal and contact, and a footer with KUYURU set large over the house details and a small sitemap. The house address, hours and shipping note, the scent-notes legend and the shelf with its prices and badge live in three synced patterns, so each is edited once (WooCommerce optional: without it the shop page shows the shelf and orders go by email).

themes.description: A quiet, crafted theme for a small ramen-ya with eight seats: washi-coloured pages, sumi ink type, dark wood and a single restrained vermilion, Shippori Mincho B1 headings over Zen Kaku Gothic New and generous white space. A linen noren split into three panels carries the shop's name at the top of every page, and the menu runs down the right edge in vertical type (a simple menu button on phones). The home page is one long read: a photograph of a steaming bowl, a short essay on the broth, the menu as a printed menu card with dotted leaders and prices, the counter, the cook's hands and a quiet note on the hours. The ink-dark footer carries a stamped vermilion seal and the hours and address as a vertical column of text. The home page runs from the dimmed cover through the family story, a featured-car forecourt ledger, three approved-used statements, a full-bleed service band, three location rows, the team on a steel band and the journal to a test-drive close. The same three techniques head every inner page: New Cars, single vehicle, Approved Used, Service, Locations, Our Team, Finance and Warranty, Test Drive, Contact, About, the journal, cart, checkout and account. themes.name: Michishirube Consulting
themes.description: Michishirube Consulting — a management consulting firm theme set as a vertical scroll: under a formal top header (firm name, tagline and a Book a first call button), the menu leaves the bar on wide screens and becomes a fixed midnight-navy side rail down the left edge with numbered entries set horizontally in every language, hairline dividers and a brass marker on the current page; phones get a full-screen navy overlay menu with large entries. Deep navy (#1E3A5F) is the main colour, chosen for trust: the hero, the story band and every page head are navy fields set in white, with mist blue-grey panels, cloud-white grounds and a muted brass accent kept to small rules and markers; in Chinese and Japanese a short vertical line beside the hero title is the only tategaki touch. The hero is a cut-out object breaking its frame: the title, lead and buttons on the left, a framed low-key photograph of an empty boardroom at dusk on the right, and a cut-out consultant (transparent WebP) standing over the frame's corner and dropping past the hero bottom edge; a cut-out brass compass breaks over the story band and every page head. Every picture is a realistic low-key photograph (50mm f/1.4, one hard window light, deep shadows) of a modern, international office. BIZ UDMincho for display, Crimson Pro for reading, Noto Serif TC for Traditional Chinese headings. Sample content in English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French and German. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
themes.deviation: 1.0.1 (issue #185): the main colour changed from shikon violet #3F2A5E to deep navy #1E3A5F for a more trustworthy look (design-plan row b5-7 updated to match), with a muted brass #C9A66B accent for small markers only; the photos were re-graded from violet to navy. The Chinese and Japanese side rail no longer sets its entries top to bottom (writing-mode vertical-rl turned it into a row of narrow columns): every language now uses the same horizontal numbered rail with a current-page marker, and zh/ja section titles are horizontal too; the only vertical text left is the short tategaki line beside the hero title. Otherwise built to design-plan.json row b5-7 (tategaki-vertical-scroll, cutout-break-frame-object hero, side-rail nav, real-photography, low-key photo direction, BIZ UDMincho + Crimson Pro, business-services). A formal top header with the firm name, tagline and the Book a first call button; on wide screens the menu becomes a fixed side rail. Break-frame: the cut-out consultant breaks out of the framed hero photo and the hero bottom edge; the cut-out brass compass breaks over the story band and page heads. Contrast: white #FFFFFF on navy #1E3A5F 11.5:1 (all text on the hero, story band, every page head, navy buttons and step badges); pale steel blue #BFD0E3 on navy 7.3:1 (labels on the fields); paper #F5F7FA on ink #0E1B2E 16.1:1 and pale steel blue on ink 11.0:1 (side rail, overlay menu, footer); ink on paper 16.1:1 and on mist #E6ECF3 14.5:1; indigo #2A5585 on paper 7.2:1 and on mist 6.5:1 (links); white on indigo 7.7:1; quiet #4A5868 on paper 6.8:1 and on mist 6.1:1; brass #C9A66B on ink 7.5:1 (current-page numeral) and on navy 5.0:1, otherwise decorative only (rail edge, header rule, current-item marker); ink is never used on navy.

themes.name: Mizuha Glass
themes.description: A serene, sculptural store theme for a small glass studio in a quiet river-mouth town, making hand-blown and kiln-formed tableware in old bottle green, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Mist pages, sage glass panels, deep ink text and a bottle-green accent; Cardo for display, Source Sans 3 for text. A transparent header lies over a full-bleed photograph of backlit glass and turns solid mist with a hairline as the page scrolls (H8; inner pages start solid); the home page moves in long pauses between two full-bleed photographs and a few calm sections (L1): the studio idea, a shelf of four pieces, how we make it (gather, blow, anneal), the shipping promise and the journal. Product cells and photo frames carry soft refraction highlights (a diagonal light streak and a faint caustic glow) drawn only with CSS gradients, and a thin glass-edge hairline. The studio and Shipping & care pages, journal, newsletter and contact; a one-line footer (F3) with the town and email from the synced studio card. The studio address, showroom hours, telephone and email, and the packing, breakage, delivery and returns policy each live in one synced pattern (the policy shows in short form on the home page, in full on Shipping & care and beside add-to-cart on every product); each product's size line is kept once as its Size attribute (WooCommerce optional: without it the shop shows a static shelf and orders go by email).
themes.deviation: Codes: none (H8 + F3 + L1 as planned; combination unused: Kaori Cosme is H10/F3/L1, Asa Linen H8/F8/L13, Undo Ba H8/F7/L12, Hana Kago H8/F4/L8). Palette as planned (mist #EEF2EC, sage glass #CFDCCB, deep ink #233026, bottle green #6E8B6A) with added colours: bottle green is 3.3:1 on mist and 2.7:1 on sage, so it is kept to large display marks, rules, step numerals, separators and the refraction tint; links, small labels and the arrow links use deep bottle green #46604A (6.1:1 on mist, 4.9:1 on sage, 6.5:1 on paper); secondary text uses quiet green-grey #4F5D53 (6.1:1 on mist, 4.9:1 on sage); body ink #233026 is 12.2:1 on mist and 9.7:1 on sage; buttons are ink with mist text (12.2:1); pale mist #F6F8F4 cards and a glass-edge hairline #B4C5AF were added. H8 differs from Asa Linen, Undo Ba and Hana Kago by a mist scrim at the top of a light backlit photograph with ink type, transparent only on the home page (inner pages start solid), fading to solid mist with a hairline via a CSS scroll timeline (script fallback; solid at once for reduced motion). F3 differs from Kaori Cosme, Kasumi Bar and Kura Shizuku as a single centred line on mist (copyright, town and email read from the synced studio card, three links) that stacks into centred lines on phones. L1 differs from Kaori Cosme, Hinoki Yado and Shashin Folio by two full-bleed glass photographs with very long pauses and a staggered three-step making row. Fonts verified against google/fonts OFL.txt: Cardo is OFL-1.1 without a Reserved Font Name (Regular, Italic and Bold subset to Latin WOFF2); Source Sans 3 carries the Reserved Font Name 'Source', so it ships unmodified as Adobe's own variable WOFF2 (SourceSans3VF-Upright.ttf.woff2, weights 200-900, from adobe-fonts/source-sans). Cardo has no tabular-figure feature, so prices use its default lining figures (font-variant-numeric set for fallbacks). Product photographs are cropped to 4:5. Added a newsletter page because check-themes requires it; industry glassware and page tag shipping-and-care are new (The studio uses the about tag).

themes.name: Nameshi Leather
themes.description: A quiet, handmade store theme for a small leather atelier in a riverside workshop district, making vegetable-tanned wallets, bags and belts by hand and repairing them for life, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Parchment pages, tan panels, ink-brown text and a saddle accent; Libre Baskerville for display, Epilogue for text. A centred Libre Baskerville wordmark between two tiny dashed stitch marks with the menu split left and right on a parchment bar, a stitched seam beneath (H2); the home page opens with a compact title block (Made to patina) and goes straight into a filter-first directory of every piece by item (wallets, bags, belts) and leather (natural, black, indigo) on stitched hairline cells, each with a new / one year / five years patina strip under its price (L14); then how leather ages, the synced repair and care promise and the journal. A split two-tone footer: the parchment workshop card beside an ink-brown band with the newsletter and links (F10). Patina guide, Repairs and The atelier pages, journal, newsletter and contact. The workshop address, hours, telephone and email, and the repair and care policy, each live in one synced pattern (WooCommerce optional: without it the directory shows static cells and orders go by email).

Palette as planned (parchment #EFE7DD, tan #C9A27E, ink brown #3A2A1F, saddle #7A5236) with added colours, all AA-checked: ink brown is 11.2:1 on parchment, 5.9:1 on tan and 12.3:1 on pale parchment; saddle is 5.6:1 on parchment (used there for labels and italic accents) but only 2.9:1 on tan, so on tan it appears only as rules and marks; deep saddle #4E321F was added for links and small text on tan (9.5:1 on parchment, 5.0:1 on tan); quiet brown #5E4A3B for secondary text, used on parchment and pale parchment only (6.8:1 / 7.5:1; 3.6:1 on tan, so tan panels use ink); pale parchment #F7F2EA cards and a seam hairline #B89878 (decorative). Buttons are ink with parchment text (11.2:1); the footer band is ink brown with parchment text (11.2:1), muted parchment #D9C7B2 labels (8.3:1) and tan links (5.9:1). H2 differs from Kuyuru, Kura, Komugi and Sakura by a stitched dashed seam under the bar and tiny dashed stitch marks either side of the centred wordmark (no pills, frames or stickers); the menu splits three left / three right with account and cart in the right cluster, and becomes a Menu button below 1180px. F10 differs from Tsuya (black/cinnabar), Ginrin (graphite/steel) and Sushi (navy/hinoki) as parchment and ink brown halves with a stitched link rule. L14 differs from Kumo (titanium eyewear cells), Sumai (ruled listings) and Neiro (ticket stubs) by stitched leather cells with a patina strip under each price. Fonts verified against google/fonts OFL.txt: Libre Baskerville carries the Reserved Font Name 'Libre Baskerville', so its two variable TTFs (Roman and Italic, weights 400-700) ship unmodified; Epilogue is OFL-1.1 without a Reserved Font Name (variable Latin WOFF2 subset, as in Tsuya Lacquer). Added a newsletter page because check-themes requires it; industry leather-goods, style crafted, colour brown and page tags patina-guide and repairs are new (The atelier uses the about tag).

The home page opens on a dark band with the empty hall, then the programme as a filter-first directory of ticket stubs (perforated edge, mono date, seat line) filtered by genre and month with accessible pill buttons; without JavaScript every concert shows. themes.name: Nijimi Tenugui
themes.description: A handmade, organic store theme for a small tenugui dye workshop by the river in the fictional town of Kawasoe, pour-dyeing (chusen) cotton tenugui cloths in indigo since 1962, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Pale indigo paper pages, an indigo wash for panels, deep indigo ink text and one muted dyer's blue; Kiwi Maru for display, Mona Sans for text. The hero and the cloth and pour pictures are calm 2D flat raster illustrations (WebP; solid shapes, no outlines, repeat-pattern feel); the four pattern swatches are small geometric SVG tiles; product pictures are photographs. A floating pill header in pale indigo carries the menu, the account link and the cart (H10). The home page is an unfolding cloth (L13): one illustration of a tenugui stays pinned on the left while the chapters scroll beside it, and it changes from folded to opened to hung as each chapter comes into view; then a shelf of four cloths, the pour (paste, pour, rinse) as a wide flat illustration, the dye notes and care, and the journal. The footer opens with a strip of four cloth patterns cropped square (F8), then the name, the menu, the workshop address and hours. Pages: Shop, Patterns (the four stencil repeats with their meanings), How to use & care, The workshop (people, the dye week, visiting), Journal, Newsletter and Contact. The workshop details and the dye notes and care each live in one synced pattern (the care card shows in short form on the home page, in full on How to use & care and beside add-to-cart on every product); each cloth's specifications are product attributes (size, dye, cotton, method, ends), and size and dye print under every price (WooCommerce optional: without it the shop shows a static shelf and orders go by email).

summary.en: A calm store for a small tenugui dye workshop: a flat illustrated cloth folds, opens and hangs as you scroll, with patterns and care.

summary.fr: Une boutique calme pour un petit atelier de tenugui : un tissu en illustration plate se plie, s'ouvre et sèche au fil du défilement.
summary.de: Ein ruhiger Shop für eine kleine Tenugui-Färberei: ein flach illustriertes Tuch faltet sich beim Scrollen auf und hängt zum Trocknen.

themes.name: Niko Kids Clinic
themes.description: Niko Kids Clinic — a theme for a paediatric clinic (illness visits, vaccinations, check-ups and an allergy clinic), laid out as an editorial magazine under a formal white top header: the clinic name and tagline centred on top, a Book a visit button at the right and the menu as a centred row underneath (an aqua numbered overlay on phones). Byakugun pale aqua (#78C2C4) is the main colour, with a fine film-grain texture: the hero field, the story band, the visit-steps heading block and every page head are aqua fields in deep-teal type, with coral as a second risograph-style ink. The hero is a diagonal split: text on the aqua field, the waiting-room photograph cut on a diagonal with a coral misregistered edge, and a photo collage across the seam — a tilted print of toy blocks, a cut-out stethoscope and a cut-out teddy bear (transparent WebP) that breaks across the diagonal and past the hero bottom edge. Sections read like a magazine: running rules over every label, a numbered two-column care index with column rules, staggered visit steps and a lead story beside two side stories. Every picture is a realistic film-grain photograph (35mm look, 50mm f/2, natural side light). Noto Sans JP for display, Lato for reading, Noto Sans TC for Traditional Chinese headings. Sample content in English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French and German; vertical labels only in Chinese and Japanese. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.

The collage is built from those photographs: a tilted print and two transparent cut-outs layered across the diagonal.

themes.name: Omocha Kendama
themes.description: Omocha Kendama — a store theme for a small wooden toy shop and turning workshop, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Sumi (#1C1C1C) is the main colour: the masthead, the hero, the feature spread, every page head and the footer are sumi fields with bone type and beech and kendama-red marks; Zen Kurenaido for display and Work Sans for reading. It is laid out like a small magazine: an issue strip in the header, a menu that opens as a full-screen overlay of numbered links, a product-grid hero of film photographs where a cut-out kendama swings out of the headline cell across the grid lines and a cut-out spinning top rises out of the last strip, then the contents of the issue, a two-column feature with a pull quote, the toy shelf and the journal. All photographs are generated in one 35mm film-grain direction graded toward sumi. The shop details and the wood-and-care notes each live in one synced pattern (WooCommerce optional: without it the toys show as static cells and orders go by email).
themes.deviation: None: built exactly to design-plan.json row b3-15 (editorial-magazine, product-grid-hero, overlay nav, real-photography images, film-grain photo direction, sumi #1C1C1C, Zen Kurenaido + Work Sans). Every picture is a photorealistic 35mm film-grain photograph generated with Grok Build and graded toward sumi; the kendama and the spinning top are also transparent cut-outs that break out of the hero grid. Contrast: bone #EEEAE2 on sumi #1C1C1C 14.2:1 (all text on the sumi masthead, hero, feature, page heads, bands and footer); ash #B9B3A8 on sumi 8.2:1; beech #D8B88A on sumi 9.0:1 (labels, buttons, drop caps; sumi on beech buttons 9.0:1); light red #E86A4E on sumi 5.4:1 (numbers and emphasis); sumi on paper #F3F1EC 15.1:1; deep red links #9C2A1C on paper 6.7:1; stone #57534B on paper 6.8:1; kendama red #C0392B on paper 4.8:1 (large numbers and marks).

The header is a programme-guide masthead: a dateline with the on-air time and a pulsing “On air” lamp, a giant wordmark across the page, then the menu on a ruled bar with a tuning-scale edge. The home page is a broadcast log: after a cover with a tuning dial, the latest episodes stand as stops on a vertical amber timeline, each with its date, the episode number, running time, a waveform that plays when pointed at and a record sleeve whose vinyl slides out; then the running order of an hour, the two hosts and a listener's letter. The footer is led by the newsletter in a full-width amber band. With a numbered Episodes index with running times, Hosts with the crew, About with a week of making an episode as a timeline, show notes, a newsletter and contact. Episode numbers and running times are written once in each episode's listen bar; the on-air time, subscribe links, email addresses and social links are each edited in one place.

The header is centred: the school's name in a pink pill in the middle, the menu split to its left and right, a row of petal dots underneath. The home page is one bento grid of rounded cells: a blue welcome, a classroom photo, the five levels, the word of the week, a teacher, the street in spring, online lessons, the free trial lesson, three numbers, the latest journal posts and a student's quote. Hiragana stickers, a single decorative kana on a tilted rounded badge, sit on the corners of cards; every readable word stays English. The footer is centred on the opening-hours table. With Courses (six course cards with prices), Levels (five levels from Seed to Canopy as a rising staircase), a Schedule with the weekly class timetable and term dates, About with the teachers, a school journal, a newsletter and contact. The opening hours, the timetable and the address, email and social links are each edited in one place.

themes.name: Shigure Umbrellas
themes.description: A quiet store theme for a small umbrella atelier on a riverside shopping street, making and mending traditional and compact umbrellas by hand, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Rain-mist pages, slate panels, ink text and one muted steel accent; Ibarra Real Nova for reading and display, Golos Text for labels and rib counts. The wordmark sits centred between two tiny ferrule tip marks with the menu split three left and three right on a pale mist bar, a cool steel hairline beneath (H2); the home page opens with one quiet line (Umbrellas for the quiet rain) and then the canopy rail, a slow sideways scroll-snap track of opened umbrellas in large round canopy cells with their rib count and width in small type, keyboard and touch scrollable (L4); then the atelier note, the synced repair promise, a size-guide teaser drawn as concentric canopy rings, and the journal. The footer leads with a rain letter sign-up on a deep slate band, with shop details and slim links below (F4). Care & repair, Size guide, The workshop, journal, newsletter and contact. The shop address, hours, telephone and email, and the repair terms, each live in one synced pattern (WooCommerce optional: without it the rail shows static canopies and orders go by email).

Palette as planned (mist #E9ECEF, slate #D3D9DF, ink #23303B, muted steel #5E7489) with added colours, all AA-checked (WCAG 2.x): ink is 11.4:1 on mist, 9.5:1 on slate and 12.6:1 on pale mist #F5F7F8; muted steel #5E7489 is only 4.1:1 on mist and 3.4:1 on slate, so it is used only for large display italics, ferrule and tip marks, canopy rings and hairlines, never for small text; deep steel #3F5263 was added for links, labels and rib counts (6.8:1 mist, 5.7:1 slate, 7.5:1 pale mist); quiet slate #4E5A66 for secondary text (6.0:1 mist, 5.0:1 slate, 6.6:1 pale mist); steel hairline #B4C0CB is decorative only; pale mist #F5F7F8 for cards. Buttons are ink with mist text (11.4:1). The F4 band is deep slate #23303B (the ink) with mist text (11.4:1) and muted labels #B4C0CB (7.3:1), chosen over a #D3D9DF band so the footer reads as one quiet dark band under airy pages. H2 differs from Komugi (warm flour), Kuyuru (wisteria), Nameshi (stitched parchment) and Sakura (pink pill): cool mist bar, one steel hairline, tiny CSS ferrule tip marks either side of the wordmark; account and cart sit in the right cluster when WooCommerce is active; below 1180px the menu becomes a Menu button and the wordmark stays centred on one line at 390px. L4 differs from Kinu (framed kimono rack), Kiroku (kinetic reel) and Amane (seasonal tray months): large round canopy cells with faint radial rib lines, no autoplay or motion, scroll-snap with keyboard focus. F4 differs from Kumo (cool grey technical), Eda (lichen letter), Hana (Monday stem letter) and Oto (amber band): a centred rain letter on deep slate with the ferrule mark. Fonts verified against google/fonts OFL.txt (2026-10-13): Ibarra Real Nova and Golos Text are OFL-1.1 with no Reserved Font Name, so both ship as Latin WOFF2 subsets (Ibarra Real Nova Roman weights 400-600, Italic 400-500, Golos Text 400-500). Ibarra Real Nova has no tabular-figure feature, so prices use its lining figures and the rib counts, table cells and step numbers use Golos Text tabular figures. Added a newsletter page because check-themes requires it; industry umbrellas and page tags care-repair and size-guide are new (The workshop uses the about tag).

themes.description: A bright, woodblock-print hospitality theme for a six-room island guesthouse. The art is ukiyo-e woodblock raster illustration (the inn, the harbour, a tatami room, a dinner tray, the coast road), with the inn and the dinner tray as transparent cut-outs that break out of their frames. The rates card and the inn details are synced patterns edited in one place. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.

themes.description: Shinai Dojo — a neighbourhood kendo dojo theme set like a magazine. A formal top header carries the dojo name and tagline, a Book a trial class button and a menu button that opens a full-screen madder red overlay with large numbered entries. Akane (#B7282E), the deep madder red of traditional Japanese dyeing, is the main colour: the cover, the dojo band and every page head are madder fields with a faint asanoha hemp-leaf pattern texture multiplied in, set in plaster white with hinoki-gold labels. The cover is a stacked collage: the issue line, title, lead, buttons and the contents of this issue on the left, three numbered 2.5D isometric plates of the dojo stacked and offset on the right, and a cut-out kendo helmet (transparent WebP) breaking out of the stack and over the cover bottom edge; a cut-out dojo drum breaks over the top edge of the dojo band and the bottom edge of every page head. The home page reads as three features: the classes as a magazine spread with a drop cap and a pull quote, the dojo story with the founding year in giant type, and a practice in four plates on pale madder with the light pattern; a synced practice board and the fees are kept in one place each. Every picture is a 2.5D isometric illustration. Shippori Antique for display, Libre Franklin for reading, Noto Sans TC for Traditional Chinese headings. Sample content in English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French and German; vertical labels only in Chinese and Japanese. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
themes.deviation: None: built exactly to design-plan.json row b4-11 (editorial-magazine, stacked-collage hero, overlay nav, pattern-texture, 2.5d-isometric, akane #B7282E, Shippori Antique + Libre Franklin, kendo dojo in education-classes). A formal top header with the dojo name, the Book a trial class button and the overlay menu button. Pattern texture: an asanoha hemp-leaf tile multiplied into every madder field and a light version on the pale madder practice band. Break-frame: the cut-out kendo helmet breaks out of the stacked plates and over the cover bottom edge, and the cut-out dojo drum over the dojo band and page heads.

themes.name: Shiori Review
themes.description: A quiet, typographic media theme for an independent literary quarterly of essays and poems. Oat paper, warm stone and sumi ink, with a faded red pencil used for thin bookmark ribbons and rules and a deeper red-brown for links. The masthead sets a huge Source Serif 4 wordmark over a dateline (issue number, season, place and cadence) and a ruled menu row; on phones the wordmark and a Menu button share one line. The home page is a contents page: the issue title and cover beside a numbered index of essays and poems, each with its author, an Essay or Poem chip and a page-like folio in Azeret Mono, with a bookmark ribbon hanging over each part; then a note from the editor, a short subscribe-and-submit note and the journal. The footer is a calm strip of issue covers over the colophon. With Issues (an archive with covers), Submissions, Subscribe, Editors, Journal, Newsletter and Contact. The magazine details and the subscription + submissions rates are each one synced pattern. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
themes.deviation: none for the header, footer and layout codes (H5 / F8 / L3 as planned). Colours as planned (oat paper #F3EFE7, warm stone #E0D8C9, sumi ink #1F1D1A, faded red pencil #6A3E35) plus: deep red-brown #5A2E26 for links, buttons' hover, chips' text and small accents (9.9:1 on oat, 8.0:1 on stone, 10.7:1 on paper), muted ink #5E574D for secondary text (6.2:1 on oat, 5.0:1 on stone, 6.7:1 on paper) and paper #FAF8F3 for detail cards. Sumi ink is 14.7:1 on oat, 11.9:1 on stone and 15.8:1 on paper. The faded red #6A3E35 passes AA too (7.8:1 on oat, 6.3:1 on stone) but is kept for the bookmark ribbons, hairline underlines, drop caps and chip borders, at 85% opacity on the ribbons.

Every picture is a photorealistic high-key photograph (85mm, softbox light, near-white ground, faint shadows, fine grain, colour graded toward sumire). A formal centred top header carries the Shop cameras button on the left, the shop name in the middle, account and cart on the right and the main menu centred on its own row below, under a strip of clay sprocket holes; below 1100 px a Menu button opens it as a full-screen mikan overlay. Mikan orange (#F08300) is the main colour: the hero field, the counter board lead tile, the camera shelf band, the darkroom card, every page head and the footer strip are mikan fields with camera-black text, and raster clay textures (film sprocket holes and a halftone of clay dots) run through them. The hero shows the clay shop interior through a black viewfinder window with rounded corners and frame marks; a cream card with the lead overlaps the window and a cut-out clay camera (transparent WebP) breaks out over the window frame and the hero's bottom edge. The counter board, the five checks, the camera shelf, the darkroom collage and the counter notes are all uneven masonry tiles and columns, and a cut-out film roll breaks out of the darkroom card. Every picture is a soft 3D clay illustration. DotGothic16 for display, Lexend Deca for reading. Sample content and products in English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French and German; vertical lines only in Chinese and Japanese. Works without WooCommerce. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.

Every page opens with a magazine masthead (a dateline row, the counter's name set large between hairlines, the menu beneath). The home page reads like a journal's contents page: a cover line and wide photograph, a numbered index of the site, the course card, the chef, the latest journal entries and the seatings. The omakase page lays the evening out in five movements, each marked by a small ringed plate from the plate legend. The footer is a two-tone split: a navy panel with the address and seatings beside a hinoki booking panel. themes.name: Suzuri Shodo
themes.description: A quiet, vertical-type education theme for a small calligraphy (shodo) school in an old timber house with a moss-garden veranda. Washi, felt grey and sumi ink, with a muted seal red used only for small marks (the active menu numeral, the free trial slot, today's timetable marker and the stopping dot after vertical titles). The wordmark sits top-left in Sawarabi Mincho; on the home page the menu is a numbered list with hairline leaders in the hero's lower-right corner, on inner pages a compact numbered row top-right. The home page is a sequence of chapters with long pauses: the hero brush-stroke photograph as a wide pale sheet with the school's idea set vertically, four chapters (ink, brush, paper, the stroke) each with one photograph, a vertical title and a short paragraph on alternating sides, the five class levels as tall vertical columns read right to left like hanging scrolls (weekly hours and monthly fees), a note from the teacher, the free trial lesson and the journal. The footer is the weekly class timetable drawn as a folded practice sheet on felt grey, with today marked from the site's timezone, beside the school details. With Classes, Timetable, Materials (the starter kit with prices and care notes), About, Journal, Newsletter and Contact (a trial-lesson enquiry that composes an email, no backend). The school details, the timetable and the class levels are synced patterns, edited once. Sawarabi Mincho over Zen Kaku Gothic Antique. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
themes.deviation: none for the header, footer and layout codes (H12 / F11 / L5 as planned). Edo purple (#745399) is the main colour: the hero, every page head and the festival band are purple fields with white type. Every picture is a low-key photograph (50mm f/1.4, hard window light, dark ground, graded toward Edo purple). Yusei Magic for display, Karla for reading. themes.description: A bold, Japanese-minimal store theme for a small milliner's atelier in Hoshikawa City: cloches, boaters, buckets and wide brims blocked by hand, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Washi pages with a faint fibre texture, large fields of edo-murasaki purple (#745399), ai indigo (#165E83) and matcha (#C5C56A), one koubai plum-blossom pink (#E16B8C) accent for the hanging tag, numerals and marks, and sumi ink; Kaisei Opti for display, M PLUS 2 for text. The header (H11) is a formal top header read left to right: a small koubai tag hangs from the top edge beside the wordmark, the menu runs horizontally with numbered items, then account and cart. The home page (L5) is an asymmetric 12-column editorial layout read horizontally, with a blank left margin column that carries only the section numbers (and the season line set vertically as a title accent): a large headline beside an etching laid over an Edo purple field, Find your shape keeps the filter-first catalogue (shape, material, head size) with the hats in an asymmetric masonry of three unequal columns, the four shapes as a ruled list on a matcha band with a cut-out hat breaking over its edge, then three steps, fit and sizing on indigo and the journal as a ruled index. The footer (F4) leads with the seasonal letter on an Edo purple band over a deep shikon base with the wordmark set vertically in koubai. Hand-tinted copperplate etching illustrations (indigo and koubai washes). Fit & sizing, Made to order, Atelier, journal, newsletter and contact. The shop card, the sizing guide and the shapes table each live in one synced pattern; material and brim print under every price (WooCommerce optional: without it the shop shows a static catalogue that filters by shape and material without JavaScript, and orders go by email).

themes.name: Tsuki Silver
themes.description: An elegant, restrained store theme for a small silver jewellery atelier, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Moonstone blush paper, muted rose panels, ink text and soft silver reflections; Sorts Mill Goudy for display, Questrial for text. A floating pearl pill header (H10) with the wordmark, menu, account and cart. The home page puts the pieces first (L11): a short title and the five product families marked by moon phases drawn in CSS (new, crescent, half, gibbous, full), then straight into a rhythmic grid of pieces on pale stone (a 2 x 2 feature, pairs of squares and one wide tile), the atelier, sizing and care, the journal and the letter. Ring sizing (four ways, a US size table, free resizing) and Care (four habits, what silver dislikes, free re-polishing) pages; atelier, journal, newsletter and contact pages. The footer (F12) is a stamped round seal and a vertical line of italic text beside the wordmark, the menu and the visit rows of the synced atelier card. The address, hours, telephone, email and the sizing and care notes live in one synced pattern used by the footer, Ring sizing, Care and Contact; every product shows its metal line, kept once as a product attribute (WooCommerce optional: without it the home grid and the shop page show the synced tray and orders go by email).
themes.deviation: Palette, fonts, style tags and H10 + F12 + L11 are as planned (combination unused: Kaori Cosme is H10/F3/L1, Hikari App H10/F2/L6, Kami no Ne H3/F12/L8, Menya Kaen H11/F12/L7, Komugi Pan H2/F8/L11, Ginrin Cycle H6/F10/L11). Muted rose #A07873 is 3.5:1 on blush (2.8:1 on the rose panel), so it is kept to moon marks, hairlines and large marks; links, labels, italic heading accents and the seal use deep rose #6E4E4A (6.6:1 on blush, 5.2:1 on the rose panel), secondary text quiet ink #5E5455 (6.5:1 on blush, 5.2:1 on the rose panel); ink #2E2A2A is 12.7:1 on blush. Pearl #FBF8F7 cards, soft silver #C9C1BF hairlines and pale rose #D9BDB8 were added. H10 differs from Kaori Cosme and Hikari App by a pearl pill with a silver edge, a crescent mark before a Goudy wordmark, centred spaced-capital menu and a rose cart chip; on phones wordmark, Menu and cart stay on one line inside the pill. F12 differs from Kami no Ne and Menya Kaen by a round SVG seal (ring text and a crescent, tilted like a stamp) in deep rose beside a vertical italic line on the muted rose panel. L11 differs from Komugi Pan and Ginrin Cycle by a moon-phase category index under a short title and a four-column grid on pale stone with a 2 x 2 feature tile and a wide tile every eight pieces, a silver sheen on hover (none with reduced motion). Both fonts verified OFL-1.1 without a Reserved Font Name (google/fonts ofl/sortsmillgoudy, ofl/questrial) and subset to Latin WOFF2 (~83 KB). The Care page uses the existing generic page tag care-guide (the existing tag care is labelled Knife care); the page itself is /care/. Industry silver-jewellery and page tag ring-sizing are new. The eighth product photo (Waning Dome Ring) is a crop of the atelier bench photograph. Added a newsletter page because check-themes requires it.

themes.name: Tsuribito Tackle
themes.description: Tsuribito Tackle — a WooCommerce store theme for a small harbour tackle shop, built as horizontal strips. A white top header carries the shop name, a Shop the tackle button, the account and cart, and a Menu button that opens a full-screen crimson overlay menu (numbered; vertical words in Chinese and Japanese). Crimson red (#C9171E) is the main colour: the strip across the hero's foot, the synced tide board, the tested-on-the-breakwater band, every page head and the footer strip are crimson fields. The hero is a full-bleed high-key photograph of a misty shore; a cut-out reel (transparent WebP) breaks out over the crimson strip and the photo edge, a cut-out red float breaks out of the shop photo and over the band's top edge, and over every page head. The shelf, the three waters, the promises and the tide notes are sideways scroll-snap strips. Every picture is a photorealistic high-key photograph. Kiwi Maru for display, Onest for reading. Sample content and products in English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French and German; vertical labels only in Chinese and Japanese. Works without WooCommerce. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
themes.deviation: None: built exactly to design-plan.json row b3-25 (horizontal-strip, full-bleed-illustration hero, overlay nav, real-photography, high-key, beni crimson #C9171E, Kiwi Maru + Onest, fishing tackle shop in shops-hobbies). A full top header (shop name, Shop the tackle button, account and cart) whose Menu button opens a full-screen crimson overlay menu at every width (numbered; vertical words in Chinese and Japanese). The full-bleed hero is a photograph, since the row's image treatment is real-photography: every picture is a photorealistic high-key photograph (85mm f/2.8, large softbox, near-white background, faint shadows, graded toward crimson) generated with Grok Build. Horizontal strips: the crimson hero strip, the tide board cells, the product shelf, the three waters, the promises and the tide notes run sideways with scroll-snap. Break-frame: the cut-out reel (transparent WebP) breaks out of the full-bleed hero photo, over the crimson strip at its foot and into the tide board below; the cut-out red float breaks out of the framed shop photo and over the top edge of the crimson breakwater band; the same float breaks over the bottom edge of every page head. Sample content and products in en, zh-TW, ja, fr and de. Contrast: white #FFFFFF on crimson #C9171E 5.79:1 (all text on the hero strip, tide board, breakwater band, page heads, footer strip, menu overlay and buttons); ink #1C1416 on white 18.1:1 (body text, hero type over the high-key photo's white sky); deep crimson #9E1117 on white 8.25:1 and on mist #F6F1F1 7.37:1 (links, prices, labels); wet stone #5F5658 on white 7.1:1 and on mist 6.34:1 (secondary text); white on ink 18.1:1 and pale red #F4B9BB on ink 10.8:1 (footer); crimson on white 5.79:1 (marks); ink on crimson only 3.1:1, never used for text.

themes.name: Tsuya Lacquer
themes.description: A luxe, restrained store theme for a small urushi lacquerware workshop, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Lacquer-black and deep brown-black bands alternate with warm ivory pages; one muted cinnabar is kept to small marks and the footer panel. Castoro for display and Epilogue for text. A hamburger-only header opens a full-screen lacquer-black overlay menu of large numbered serif items; the home page opens on a full-bleed photograph of a glossy black bowl. Product photographs carry a soft, still gloss highlight, and every product shows its layers-of-lacquer count, kept once as a product attribute. The Craft explains each coat, the Care guide how to live with lacquer; workshop, journal and contact pages. A split black and cinnabar footer holds the workshop details. The workshop address, hours and email, and the fallback shelf with prices and badge, live in synced patterns so each is edited once (WooCommerce optional: without it the shop page shows the shelf and orders go by email).
themes.deviation: Palette, fonts, style tags and H4 + F10 + L1 are as planned (combination unused). The muted cinnabar #8E3B2E is 6.6:1 on the ivory ground (AA for small text, used for links and labels) and ivory on cinnabar is 5.9:1 (footer panel), but it is only 2.2:1 on lacquer black, so on dark bands and the overlay menu small marks use a lighter cinnabar #C98371 (6.0:1 on #141211). Pale ivory #F5F0E8, sand #D8CEC0 and umber #5C524B (6.0:1) were added for panels, rules and quiet text. Both fonts verified OFL-1.1 in google/fonts (ofl/castoro, ofl/epilogue; no Reserved Font Name); variable fonts instanced to Castoro 400-500 and Epilogue 300-600 and subset to Latin WOFF2.

themes.name: Urushi Nuri
themes.description: Urushi Nuri — a WooCommerce store theme for a small urushi lacquerware workshop, laid out like an app with a side rail. A white top header carries the workshop name, the account, the cart and a Shop the lacquerware button; on wide screens the main menu runs down a fixed seiheki side rail under it (numbered; a vertical line in Chinese and Japanese), and below 1100 px it opens as a seiheki panel. Seiheki blue-green (#478384) is the main colour: the hero, the side rail, the drying-room band, every page head and the footer strip are seiheki fields; the pages sit on pale celadon with white app panels. The hero is a scene map: an isometric drawing of the workshop with five numbered pins and a legend; a cut-out vermilion bowl (transparent WebP) breaks out of the map frame and a cut-out jubako breaks over the hero's bottom edge and out of the drying-cabinet frame into the band's top edge. Every picture is a 2.5D isometric illustration. Zen Maru Gothic for display, Manrope for reading. Sample content and products in English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French and German; vertical labels only in Chinese and Japanese. Works without WooCommerce. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
themes.deviation: None: built exactly to design-plan.json row b3-28 (sidebar-app, scene-map hero, side-rail nav, cutout-break-frame, 2.5d-isometric, seiheki #478384, Zen Maru Gothic + Manrope, urushi lacquerware workshop in crafts-homeware). A formal white top header (workshop name, account, cart, Shop the lacquerware button). Side rail: from 1100 px the main menu runs down a fixed seiheki column under the header (numbered, with the opening hours; a vertical line in Chinese and Japanese); below 1100 px it opens from a menu button as a seiheki panel. Sidebar-app: the pages sit on pale celadon with white app panels and status cards (workshop board, shelf, stages, notes). Scene-map hero: an isometric drawing of the workshop with five numbered pins and a legend. Break-frame: the cut-out vermilion bowl (transparent WebP) breaks out of the framed workshop map at its top-right corner and over the seiheki hero field; the cut-out jubako breaks over the hero's bottom edge into the workshop board, and a second jubako breaks out of the framed drying-cabinet drawing and over the top edge of the seiheki band; the bowl breaks over the bottom edge of every page head. Every picture is a 2.5D isometric raster illustration generated with Grok Build. Sample content and products in en, zh-TW, ja, fr and de. Contrast: white #FFFFFF on seiheki #478384 4.3:1, used only for large text (hero and page-head titles at 36 px and up, the hero's vertical line, rail menu items and the overlay menu in 20 px bold and larger, board label 24 px, page-head leads and the footer line in 20 px bold); every smaller label on seiheki sits on a pale chip: deep seiheki #24585A on paper #F3F7F6 7.4:1 (eyebrows, rail label, opening hours, breadcrumbs, rail numbers); body text sits on white panels: ink #0F2222 on white 16.5:1 and on mist #DDEBE8 13.5:1; deep seiheki on white 8.0:1 and on mist 6.5:1 (links, prices, labels, buttons: white on deep 8.0:1); slate #475B5B on white 7.2:1 and on mist 5.9:1 (secondary text); shu vermilion #A6382A on white 6.5:1 (small marks; white on shu 6.5:1 cart badge); white on ink 16.5:1 and pale seiheki #BFE0DB on ink 11.7:1 (footer, map legend, rail hours); ink on seiheki only 3.8:1 and paper on seiheki 4.0:1, never used for small text.

themes.description: A quiet, editorial and geometric portfolio theme for a small graphic, advertising and web design studio taking client work. Cool paper white, light grey and ink, with muted ochre only for printer's crop marks and registration targets. A magazine masthead (a thin dateline with the studio's founding year, disciplines and availability, a large Hedvig Letters Serif wordmark and a ruled menu row) opens every page. The home page sets a short statement on a faint baseline grid, then the selected work as an asymmetric mosaic of project cards with crop marks and numbered figure captions, the packages, the four-stage process in one line, the team and the journal. The footer is a wide "Have a brief? Start a project" band over the studio details. With a filterable Work page (All, Graphic, Advertising, Web; every project shows without JavaScript), six case studies, Services and prices, Process, a Start a project brief form that composes an email (no backend), About, Journal, Newsletter and Contact. The studio details and the packages are synced patterns, edited once. Hedvig Letters Serif over Geist, Geist Mono for figure numbers. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.

themes.name: Yoru Chocolate
themes.description: A bold, quiet store theme for a small bean-to-bar chocolatier working at night in a former print shop on Kanzaki-dōri, Hoshikawa City: single-origin bonbons, tablets and gift boxes, with WooCommerce templates styled to match. Iron-navy (tetsukon) pages with washi fibres, kinari text, washi-light sections and one full yamabuki-yellow band; Kaisei Decol for display, BIZ UDPGothic for text. English is always set horizontally: the Japanese feel comes from asymmetric columns, hairline spines with big 01/02 numerals and staggered tall pictures; on a Chinese, Japanese or Korean site the titles, menu and captions switch to vertical writing (tategaki). The header (H11) is a top band with the wordmark, an Order a box button, account and cart, and from 1100 px the menu sits in a rail on the right edge as a clean stacked list with hairline rules and a dot on the current page; the home page (L5) opens on a large title beside a tall maki-e lacquer drawing of a moon over a box of bonbons, then puts every section title in a right-hand column behind a hairline spine: eight pieces as staggered tall strips, the four origins in ruled columns on yamabuki, the shop window at night, roast-grind-temper stepping down the page, gift boxes on washi and the journal in three ruled columns. The footer (F1) sets Yoru huge over a yamabuki moon on washi. Origins and Gift boxes pages, journal, newsletter and contact. The shop details, the warm-weather shipping note and the origins table each live in one synced pattern; cacao and origin print under every price (WooCommerce optional: without it the shop shows a static shelf and orders go by email).

summary.zh-TW: 為小型 bean-to-bar 巧克力工坊打造的沉靜商店主題：夾心巧克力、產地表與夏季寄送說明。
summary.en: A quiet, dark store for a small bean-to-bar chocolatier, with bonbons, an origins table and a warm-weather shipping note.
summary.ja: 小さなビーントゥバーのショコラティエのための静かなストア。ボンボン、産地表、夏季の発送案内付き。
summary.fr: Une boutique calme et sombre pour un petit chocolatier bean-to-bar, avec bonbons, table des origines et note d'expédition estivale.
summary.de: Ein ruhiger, dunkler Shop für einen kleinen Bean-to-Bar-Chocolatier, mit Pralinen, Herkunftstabelle und Sommerversandhinweis.

CSS only, importer and demo content untouched. 1.1.1 (themes issue #80): the right rail now holds only the vertical menu (fluid width, padding and column gaps; long menus wrap into a second tier) and a top band with the wordmark, an Order a box button, account and cart is the header on every width; codes unchanged (H11/F1/L5). 1.1.0 redesign (themes issue #66): archetype tategaki vertical scroll; H3/F1/L11 became H11/F1/L5 (combo unused; neighbours #6 Hogusu H9/F7/L7 and #8 Asagao H5/F10/L12 share no code). Palette slugs kept from 1.0 with new values: tetsukon #17184B pages, yoru night #0F1035 rail and night bands, kinari #F4EFE3 text (14.4:1 on tetsukon), yamabuki #F8B500 accent and band (9.1:1 on tetsukon; tetsukon text on yamabuki 9.1:1), light yamabuki #FFCB45 links, washi #EDE6D3 light sections (tetsukon text 13.3:1), usuzumi #5A5878 quiet text on washi (5.4:1), fuji grey #B9B6CC quiet text on navy (8.4:1). Yamabuki is never used as text on washi (1.45:1); there it marks emphasis as sesame dots. Fonts: Kaisei Decol (Regular, Bold) and BIZ UDPGothic (Regular, Bold) are OFL-1.1 without a Reserved Font Name, subset to Latin WOFF2 in assets/fonts. Illustrations: maki-e lacquer style (gold and yamabuki lacquer on navy) from Grok Build image_gen via scripts/grok-image.sh; the washi texture is a greyscale crop of one generated sheet. 1.0 image names are kept (redrawn in place) so already-imported pages keep working; 1.0 class names keep their styles.

themes.name: Yose Rakugo
themes.description: Yose Rakugo — A rakugo theatre theme set as a typographic poster in kincha golden amber (#C47222), the main colour on the header, the tall vertical banner of the hero, the full-width bill band and every page head, against riso indigo ink (#121433) and programme paper; Shippori Antique B1 display over Inter Tight. The art is risograph raster illustration (two-colour kincha and indigo riso ink with grain and misregistration): a storyteller kneeling on his cushion and an open fan as transparent cut-outs that break out of the banner, the section edges and a card, plus the kōza stage, a laughing audience, the props and the street at dusk. A full top header with the hall name centred, the menu centred beneath it between ink rules, and a Book seats button. Vertical Japanese only on Japanese text; English always runs horizontally. The door prices and the theatre details are synced patterns edited in one place. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
themes.deviation: None: built exactly to design-plan.json row b3-13 (poster-typographic, vertical-banner hero, centered nav, cutout-break-frame images, risograph illustration, kincha #C47222, Shippori Antique B1 + Inter Tight). Contrast: riso indigo #121433 on kincha #C47222 4.9:1 (all text on the kincha header, banner, bill band and page heads); white on indigo 17.9:1; lantern glow #F2B66B on indigo 10.0:1; indigo on paper #FBF1E2 16.0:1; burnt kincha #8A4A10 on paper 6.1:1; white on burnt kincha 6.9:1; quiet #5A4636 on paper 7.9:1; white never on kincha (3.6:1).

themes.name: Yuge Sento
themes.description: A serene, airy hospitality theme for a family-run neighbourhood bathhouse (sento), told as one single-column long read through an evening at the bath. Pale tile, misty blue and blue ink with a slate blue used only for numerals, rules and marks; a deeper blue for links and buttons. A slim bar docked at the bottom of the screen holds the Zen Antique Soft wordmark, the menu and today's hours with an Open now / Closed · opens 15:00 / Closed today chip worked out on the server from the site's timezone; on phones it is the wordmark, the chip and a Menu button that opens a full-screen menu read from the bottom up. The home page is a centred reading column: the opening with this evening's hours, five chapters (the curtain, the tiles, the mural, the water, cold milk after) each a short essay and one photograph, a word from the keeper, tonight's prices and the journal, divided by a small three-tile mark. The footer is a tiled waterline over a quiet street plan with the bathhouse marked by its steaming chimney, beside the address card. A faint bath-tile grid texture runs through the bar, the price card and the menu. With An evening, Bath guide (five customs, what to bring), Prices (passes, bring your own), Journal, Newsletter and Visit (a message form that composes an email, no backend). Hours, closed day, address, phone and email are edited once in Appearance > Bath details; the price list is one synced pattern. Zen Antique Soft over Be Vietnam Pro. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
themes.deviation: none for the header, footer and layout codes (H7 / F6 / L7 as planned). Colours as planned (tile #EEF2F5, misty #C9D6E0, blue ink #22323F, slate blue #5F7F96) plus: deep blue #2E5470 for links, buttons, the open chip and small text (7.1:1 on tile, 5.4:1 on misty), quiet slate #4A5A66 for secondary text (6.3:1 on tile, 4.8:1 on misty) and foam #F7F9FB for the price card, the plan and form fields. Blue ink is 11.7:1 on tile and 8.9:1 on misty. Slate blue #5F7F96 is 3.8:1 on tile and 2.9:1 on misty, so it is used only for large display numerals, rules, the three-tile mark, the today marker and the plan's bathhouse mark, never for body text.

themes.name: Yui Credit Union
themes.description: Yui Credit Union — a business theme for a member-owned credit union. A floating white rounded header bar with outlined pills and one solid pine pill, ruled ledger heads (a hairline, a numbered capital label and one pine italic word) above every section, and a uniform 3:2 pickup row with captions under a rule. A stone ground with white panels, ink text and one small pine accent. The home page opens on an inset branch photograph with the headline below, then continues with ownership, a sample-rate table, a loan calculator, what members use, a member story, the join steps, governance, branches and the journal. Merriweather for headings, Public Sans for reading. Works without any plugin. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.

themes.name: Yukimi Kakigori
themes.description: Yukimi Kakigori — a kakigori shaved-ice parlour theme built on sticky media: on wide screens the picture column holds still while the text column scrolls past it (the menu, the four bowl rows, the story band and the parlour page). A formal top header, centred: the parlour name and tagline in the middle of the first row, the menu centred on the second row and the Reserve a seat button at the right end; an overlay menu on phones and tablets. Sora-iro, the clear pale sky blue of traditional Japanese colour names (#A9D3E8), is the main colour: the hero, the story band, every page head and the overlay menu are solid ice-blue fields set in deep blue ink, on an ice-white ground with pale ice-mist panels and deep lake-blue links, cool and fresh like a bowl of shaved ice; the red of the strawberry bowl and the peach of the white-peach bowl are the only warm notes. The hero is a product grid: the title, lead, buttons and today's ice on the left, four paper-cut bowls as a taped, slightly tilted 2 x 2 collage on the right, and a cut-out bowl of strawberry ice (transparent WebP) standing in front of the grid and breaking over the hero bottom edge; a cut-out plover flag breaks over the story band and every page head. Every picture is a layered paper-cut illustration in a torn, taped paper collage. Darumadrop One for display, Rubik for reading, Noto Sans TC for Traditional Chinese headings. Sample content in English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French and German; vertical labels only in Chinese and Japanese. WCAG AA colours; no entrance animations.
themes.deviation: v1.0.2 recolour (2026-10-17): the main colour is now sora-iro, a clear pale sky ice blue #A9D3E8, with deep blue ink #12263A, an ice-white ground and ice-mist panels, for the cool, fresh feel of a shaved-ice parlour (the design plan palette family is now blue, and the unbuilt rows b4-10 and b4-12 swapped palettes to keep the window rule); the sample garden is now a snowy pond garden with a white plum tree, and eight pictures were regenerated in the new palette. Otherwise built to design-plan.json row b4-8 (sticky-media, product-grid-hero, centered nav, collage, paper-cut, Darumadrop One + Rubik, food-drink). A formal top header with the parlour name, a centred menu row and the Reserve a seat button. Sticky media on wide screens: the menu intro and ice-block picture, each bowl picture on The menu, the story collage and the parlour picture hold still while the text scrolls. Break-frame: the cut-out bowl breaks over the hero bottom edge and the cut-out plover flag over the story band and page heads.

themes.name: Yuzu Chaya
themes.description: A quiet, editorial theme for small Japanese tea and wagashi shops that sell loose-leaf sencha, hojicha and matcha, teaware and seasonal sweets online: washi paper and kinari surfaces, sumi ink, sencha green and roasted hojicha brown with a single dot of yuzu, large still-life photography, Shippori Mincho titles over Hanken Grotesk text, hairline rules and a deliberate twelve-column grid with generous whitespace that folds to one calm column on a phone, plus a brewing guide with temperatures and times, a monthly tea box subscription with plans and a signup form, and WooCommerce shop, product, cart, checkout and account templates styled to match.
